Defense mechanisms. Unconscious psychological strategies the mind deploys to protect the ego from distressing thoughts, feelings, or impulses. Theorized by Sigmund Freud, they operate automatically to reduce anxiety and maintain psychological equilibrium when the ego faces internal or external threats. Understanding defense mechanisms remains central to psychoanalytic theory and modern psychology. While Freud's theory has been challenged and refined, the core insight that people unconsciously manage unwanted emotions has proven remarkably durable and continues to inform contemporary clinical practice.

Defense mechanisms operate unconsciously. A person typically does not recognize they are employing them. They are deployed by the ego to mediate conflict between the id's impulses and the superego's restrictions. Repression is the most fundamental mechanism—burying unacceptable thoughts or memories in the unconscious. Projection attributes one's own unacceptable impulses to others. Sublimation channels unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities like aggression into sports. Rationalization constructs logical-sounding but false justifications for behavior. Denial simply refuses to acknowledge distressing reality.

They range from more primitive in younger children or severe stress to more mature forms like humor and altruism. Reaction formation converts unacceptable impulses into their opposites, unconscious hatred expressed as exaggerated affection. Intellectualization uses abstract reasoning to avoid emotional pain. Compartmentalization keeps contradictory thoughts or feelings in separate mental spaces, preventing cognitive dissonance. Displacement redirects emotional impulses toward a safer target.

Defense mechanisms are hierarchically organized. Mature defenses like humor and sublimation are more adaptive than primitive ones like denial and projection. They are central to psychoanalysis, where the framework explains how the ego mediates conflict. The unconscious mind is where they work outside awareness. Anxiety is the emotional state they aim to reduce. Talk therapy is where analysis of defense mechanisms occurs, helping make visible what operates in the patient-therapist dynamic.
